description: Behaviours section 7 names that this qualification cannot reach, each with the reason and whose they are. A qualification that left these out would read as though it had covered them.

unreachable.what: A desktop-bound session whose desktop probe runs while the session is held takes longer than the 250 ms a launch hold is given, so the held input reaches the terminal late and a reader's answer or a detach waits behind the probe.
unreachable.why_here: The probe, the supervision loop and the session lock are the worker's, in crates/kr-worker/src/runtime.rs and crates/kr-worker/src/desktop/. This suite drives a package against a bridge endpoint and starts no worker, so there is no session lock here to hold.
unreachable.next_step: Split the watch into one call that says what reading is wanted and one that folds a reading in, take the reading off the session lock, and assert that a desktop-bound session with a fence hold armed and a probe slower than the hold still delivers the held input at its own deadline.

unreachable.what: A managed session waiting for a reader's launch answer reports no demand, so a host with sleep inhibition enabled can suspend while a shell.launch is in flight and the action window can expire across the sleep.
unreachable.why_here: The scan is the control daemon's, in crates/kr-controller/src/service.rs, and the count it would read is a field on the session summary in kr-protocol. Neither is this crate, and this suite runs no daemon.
unreachable.next_step: Report how many launch confirmations a session is still waiting on, count it into the demand scan, and assert the demand before the revocation, after it, after the reader's answer and after a bridge loss.

unreachable.what: A native module of the person's own that loads into the shell and binds into an editor of an incompatible ABI, where the loader accepts the object and the mismatch is found at the point the integration reads it rather than at the point the file is opened.
unreachable.why_here: The corpus ships fixtures, and a module of that kind is a shared object compiled against one release of a shell's own headers. Building one needs a compiler and those headers on every host the qualification runs on, and it is a different object on each platform, so what the native-module cases ship is a file the loader refuses and what they qualify is the diagnosis.
unreachable.next_step: Build the module from source as part of the package build, beside the shell it is for, keep it out of the corpus as a fixture, and have the native-module cases load the built object and assert what the loader and the integration each say about it.
